claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing product (fee-simple multifamily real estate, e.g., the 222-unit Fort Wayne community) crossed the ownership boundary from unaffiliated third-party sellers asset-by-asset, while the operating processes that run it did NOT transfer from the seller — the slice states "No transitional-services, shared-services, or operating agreement with the property seller is described" and the asset was "placed directly into the Company's own, already-standing external-management structure rather than bridged by an interim arrangement." gap_mitigated=no because that product-vs-process mismatch was explicitly NOT absorbed via any transitional or operating agreement with the seller. gap_56=0: processes (T5) were not transferred or re-engineered from any counterparty at all — operations and personnel were supplied throughout by the entity's own standing sponsor-affiliated advisor and property manager, so no T5-without-T6 mismatch arises. collapse_state=T1=T6 reflects the documented fusion of controlling sponsor principal Rodney F. Emery with the officer (chairman/CEO) tier of the managed entity.

gemini.rationale: The slice documents that the customer-facing product (multifamily real estate) was acquired from third-party sellers, meaning T4 transferred. However, the operational processes and personnel (T5, T6) were not inherited from the seller but supplied by the buyer's standing external manager, creating a structural gap between the acquired asset and its former operations (gap_45=1). Neither T5 nor T6 transferred, so there is no gap between them (gap_56=0), and no transitional services agreement was used to mitigate the product-process gap.

openai.rationale: The June 3, 2014 acquisition transferred the fee-simple interest in the 222-unit multifamily property, while the slice states that operational processes and personnel were supplied by the buyer’s already-standing external advisor and property manager rather than inherited from the seller. Thus, the product crossed into ownership with a coherently aligned buyer-side operating structure, so no T4–T5 gap is documented; those processes were also run by the buyer’s established management organization, so no T5–T6 gap is documented. No transitional-services, shared-services, or seller operating agreement was described.
